subject: Request: latest security assessment for Hosted API & secure handover
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-retail.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: latest penetration assessment for Hosted API

Hi Diego,

We're preparing to complete our SIG inventory and need the most recent external penetration test or executive summary that covers Redwood's Hosted API (public endpoints, auth flows, and S3-backed object storage used for customer uploads). Can you confirm whether a report exists that includes the hosted API surface?

If you can share the report, we'd prefer an encrypted transfer or a short-lived link. Also let us know whether the report contains any customer-sensitive data that should be redacted prior to sharing.

Thanks — Jane
Jane Doe
Sr. Infosec Analyst, Acme Retail Co.
security@acme-retail.com

--
This request is part of our supplier assurance. Please advise if we need an NDA first.

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-retail.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: latest penetration assessment for Hosted API

Hi Jane — thanks for the note.

Short answer: yes, we have a June 2026 third-party assessment that covers the Hosted API surface (auth flows, public endpoints, and our S3 handling). The full PDF is treated as confidential. We can share an encrypted executive summary right away and provide controlled access to the full report via one of the following handover methods:

- Ephemeral presigned S3 object (24h expiry) plus an envelope key delivered over a separate channel.
- Temporary SFTP account with time-limited credentials and IP restriction for your security team.
- Access to our secure evidence portal (read-only) for users with a short-lived SSO invite.

Notes on redaction: the report does not include customer PII, but there are a couple of screenshots that reference internal tenant IDs; we can deliver a redacted copy if you'd like.

Can you confirm your preference (presigned S3 vs SFTP vs portal)? If you need an NDA before the full report, tell us and we'll route it to legal.

I'll attach a short handover playbook with the steps for each method.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Diego@redwood.ai

Attachments: handover-playbook-steps.txt

--

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest penetration assessment for Hosted API

Diego — looping in some infra/security details. A couple of operational points to include in the reply to Acme:

1) For presigned S3: we rotate the KMS envelope key every 24 hours and will generate a presigned URL with a 12- to 24-hour window depending on Acme's preference. We should also restrict the presigned URL to the requestor IP if they provide it.

2) For SFTP: we prefer using our staging jumpbox with ephemeral accounts; after upload we rotate credentials and delete the account. We can lock it to Acme IPs and provide an audit log export.

3) Portal: read-only access requires SAML SSO mapping; it takes about 48 hours to set up for a new domain.

Redaction: security team recommends a light redaction sweep (tenant IDs/screenshots) prior to sharing the full PDF. Executive summary (1-2 pages) can go out without redaction.

I attached a one-page checklist for the handover and the PGP public key fingerprints we use for envelope key exchange.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Field Security Operations
Lauren@redwood.ai

Attachments: redaction-checklist.txt, pgp-fingerprints.txt

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-retail.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latest penetration assessment for Hosted API & secure handover

Hi Jane — based on the options above, we recommend the presigned S3 handover (fastest) with IP lock and a 24-hour presign expiry. Proposed plan:

1) We'll upload an encrypted copy of the full assessment to a restricted S3 bucket. File name: redwood-pt-executive-summary-2026-06.pdf.enc
2) We'll generate a presigned GET URL (24h expiry) and send it to the Acme security email.
3) We'll deliver the AES-256 envelope key via a separate channel: either a PGP-encrypted email to your security address or a short SMS to an identified security contact. Please confirm the channel and the contact for the key exchange.
4) If you prefer redaction before we upload the full PDF, we can instead share the executive summary immediately and schedule redaction work; redaction usually takes 1 business day.

For compliance tracking, we will also provide an audit export (who downloaded the object, IP, timestamp) and a short remediation status summary for any outstanding items found in the assessment. Current remediation status: low/medium items mostly closed; two medium items (CORS misconfiguration on a non-production staging subdomain and a third-party dependency update) are pending with expected closure by 2026-09-10. We'll include that in the handover notes.

Please reply with: (A) presigned vs SFTP vs portal, (B) preferred envelope-key channel and contact, (C) whether you need an NDA signed before the full report.

Thanks,
Diego

--
